title: Understand SMS consent, opt-outs and text allowances
summary: Know why a notification may be stopped even when SMS is enabled.

sections.title: Channel choice and consent work together
sections.body:
SMS requires the client’s explicit selection and valid recorded consent. Public booking does not preselect SMS. A client’s channel preference alone does not establish every required consent or permit marketing.

Recognized STOP requests suppress SMS. The client can use a supported START or UNSTOP request to release that suppression; staff must not bypass it by repeatedly changing a profile checkbox. Clearing a communication channel also stops queued messages for that channel.

sections.title: What messages are supported?
sections.body:
Essential updates cover booking confirmation or approval outcomes, material changes or cancellation, payment receipts, one normal reminder, requested waitlist openings and deliberately requested queue-turn alerts.

A routine booking does not create marketing permission. Automated promotional feedback or rebooking campaigns, WhatsApp and a two-way marketing inbox are not offered in this release. Deposit-request and deposit-received notifications are not connected as an active self-service notification workflow.

sections.title: Why text units differ from message count
sections.body:
The included SMS allowance belongs to the subscription and is pooled for the business. Annual subscriptions still have monthly allowance windows. A text may use multiple units because message length and characters can produce multiple segments.

Review the allowance shown in **Client notifications** and **Subscription & billing**. No unlimited texting or hidden automatic overage is promised. A stopped, failed or simulated message should be interpreted using its history rather than counted as a confirmed customer receipt. If units are exhausted, ask the owner to review the available subscription options; do not promise an unapproved text pack or an automatic purchase.
